messages:
sam_support: heads up — customer 'EchoHealth' opened an escalation. After they pinned a model variant, their downstream pipeline started failing with embedding size mismatch (was 1536, now 1024).

customer_carlo: we pinned to redwood/emb-v2@pin-2024-11-11 around 2024-11-11 22:00 UTC. all batch jobs that process embeddings crash the reshape assertion. single-item test sometimes shows 1024, sometimes 1536.

sam_support: can you paste a minimal request+response you saw? any SDK or curl? also which region and whether you're on Hosted or Dedicated?

customer_carlo: hosted-us-east, SDK (python). example:```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood/emb-v2@pin-2024-11-11", input=["doc1","doc2"])
# resp.data[0].embedding length -> 1024 for doc1, 1536 for doc2 sometimes
```

anya_ml: thanks. two quick hypotheses: 1) the pin resolved to a variant with a different vector width (e.g., a quantized 1024 variant), or 2) routing produced a mixed-batch across variants (bad). are they using batchpad or custom batching?

customer_carlo: they use the client default batching (we send 64-doc requests via our ingestion job), batchpad=true in our pipeline.

mike_infra: @deploy-bot can you dump the model->variant mapping for customer EchoHealth and the global alias for redwood/emb-v2? want to confirm if pin mapping points to a 1024 variant.

deploy-bot: mapping dump: 
- customer:echohealth -> redwood/emb-v2@pin-2024-11-11 -> variant: emb-v2-1024-quant
- global alias redwood/emb-v2 -> emb-v2-1536-default (canary replaced earlier this week)

anya_ml: ah — mapping shows customer pinned to a 1024 quantized build. That explains consistent 1024 single-item calls, but not interleaved 1536 results in the same batch.

sam_support: customer says some items in the same batch return 1536 — any idea how a single batch would hit two variants?

mike_infra: likely cause: during batching we multiplex requests across warm workers. If serving pool contains both variants (old default + new quantized pinned variant) and routing doesn't enforce per-pin worker affinity before batch coalescing, a batch could be assembled from different workers. I can look at routing logs.

sam_support: customer provided logs with request ids. attaching snippet:```
[ingest] req_id=abc123 batching_id=b1 -> worker=wt-11 model_meta=emb-v2-1536-default
[ingest] req_id=abc124 batching_id=b1 -> worker=wt-17 model_meta=emb-v2-1024-quant
[runtime] batch b1 -> combined embeddings returned [1536, 1024]
```

anya_ml: that log proves it. Mixed-variant batch. Root cause: pin applied at control plane but serving affinity/routing didn't enforce variant homogeny for a batch. This is an edge case with batchpad and cross-worker coalescing.

jess_ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the customer's pin to the 1536 variant (map customer to emb-v2-1536-explicit), 2) force single-variant batching by setting batch_coalesce=off for that customer temporarily, or 3) move them to Dedicated so variant mix can't occur. Which does customer want?

customer_carlo: we'd like immediate rollback to previous behavior (1536) while you fix the routing — we can't change our pipeline overnight.

mike_infra: creating INF-5432 to track. Will push mapping change and trigger serving sync.

deploy-bot: performed mapping change: customer:echohealth -> emb-v2-1536-explicit at 1777777788. Service sync queued.

jess_ops: rolled mapping and forced a sync to serving pools for EchoHealth's tenant. We also added a debug flag to keep logs of batch constituent worker ids for 24h.

customer_carlo: re-tested: single-item now returns 1536 consistently. Large batch test in progress, will report. Thanks.

anya_ml: longer-term fix: ensure pin resolution and serving routing guarantee single-variant batches for pinned customers (we should never coalesce across variants for a single logical batch id). I'll add a design issue and link to INF-5432.

mike_infra: noted. also checking whether autoscale created heterogeneous pools because a new quantized image was deployed last week; adding a serving compatibility check to deployment pipeline.

sam_support: customer asked for a short summary they can give their SREs. I'll DM a concise timeline and mitigation steps.

customer_carlo: appreciate the quick turnaround. please keep us posted on root-cause and timeline for permanent fix.

sam_support: closing loop for now; INF-5432 assigned to mike_infra and anya_ml. will follow up in this thread when there's a permanent fix. :thumbsup:
